answer.rationale: Need an 18% TCO cut without raising delivery risk on a 94% loaded line with no buffer and a hard expiry in 14 days (no auto-renew). Incumbent refused a mid-cycle reopen, but renewal is the window where c4 says benchmarking still moved price and terms; c6 says a longer commitment can unlock volume pricing without cutting scope—together the only cost path that keeps the current integration (c1). Switching on c2’s low-cost/quick-onboard claim would be a primary cutover with no buffer inside two weeks and would increase delivery risk. Deferral is not analogous to c5 (that case was non-critical and continued month-to-month). Adding a second source does not replace the expiring primary and would consume the single decision. Uncertain whether 18% is achievable and whether talks can close before lapse; flag that slippage starves the line.
